facts.text: Shippagan was founded in 1790 by Jean Mallet and Marie Josephte Duguay as part of the Charles Robin Company’s expansion.
The name Shippagan first appeared in 1656 when missionary Ignatius of Paris wrote about a post called “Cibaguensi,” a Latinized form of the name.
In 1981 the town officially adopted the colloquial French spelling Shippagan, while the surrounding parish kept the original English spelling.
Shippagan sits on the Acadian Peninsula, and a bridge‑causeway links it to Lamèque Island to the northeast.
Nearly all residents—about 99%—are Francophone, reflecting the town’s strong Acadian heritage in everyday life.
Shippagan hosts campuses of Université de Moncton and New Brunswick Community College, making it a local education hub.
